title: Crucible Management Hub — Terminal UI/UX Contract

repos_in_scope.tech: Shell CLI (terminal UI/UX contract only — no implementation)

goal: Define the complete terminal interaction contract for a management hub CLI that fronts Crucible's existing symlink-based deployment (today: all-or-nothing via deploy.sh) with selective install/uninstall, dependency-aware resolution, account management, and an aggregated health view — usable equally by a human at an interactive terminal and by an agent driving it non-interactively, with zero capability gap between the two. This spec fixes what the user/agent sees and types; it fixes nothing about how the tool is built.
non_goals: "Explain/show" (a component's own description on request) — explicitly cut
Any implementation/architecture decision: file layout, script/language choice, how symlink state is diffed, how core/conditional-shared tier membership is stored
The visual theme/palette (exact hex values, box-drawing set, TUI framework choice) — except the four semantic hues (+ blue, - red, checkmark green, !/~ yellow), which are in-scope and meaning-bearing
Exact command/binary name and flag spelling — illustrative only, including --confirm=UNINSTALL
Reimplementing GitHub/Jira auth — this hub is a thin front over procedure-git-auth/procedure-jira-auth

exposes: Nine capabilities: selective install, selective uninstall, install all, uninstall all (incl. CLAUDE.md backup/restore + typed-phrase critical confirmation), dependency-aware resolution, list, account management (GitHub/Jira), doctor, dual-mode operation (interactive + agent-facing)
Three-tier component classification: core (implicit, always-on, never selectable), conditional-shared (auto-pulled via two triggers — DEV-SIDE and REVIEWER-SIDE), optional (name-pattern-discoverable)
A hard no-flags-in-the-interactive-UI wall: no CLI flag syntax in any interactive prompt/menu/confirmation/Result screen/Doctor suggestion — flags exist only in the separate agent-facing mode

A global navigation model: 'q' quits from anywhere, 'b'/'back' goes back one level, '?' opens help — with three named exceptions (pending-selection discard guard, the typed-phrase field's literal characters, the help screen closing on any key)
A glyph & color legend with ASCII fallback: checkmark=green success, x=red failure, !=yellow warning, +=blue new, -=red remove, ~=yellow re-sync, arrow=cyan informational
A three-tier confirmation ladder: Safe (default-Yes), Dangerous (default-No), Critical (typed exact phrase, 3 attempts then auto-cancel)
A closed HUB_STATUS/HUB_BLOCKED_REASON vocabulary for agent-facing mode: HUB_STATUS in {ok, blocked}; HUB_BLOCKED_REASON in {dependents_present, confirmation_required}
Dynamic discovery of optional components by naming pattern — no hardcoded component lists or counts; every specific count in the spec is one internally-consistent worked example
Full human/agent parity — no interactive action lacks a non-interactive flag equivalent
consumes: The existing deploy.sh all-or-nothing symlink-based deployment mechanism this hub fronts
procedure-git-auth / procedure-jira-auth for the underlying GitHub/Jira authentication this hub's Accounts screen manages

Terminal UX precedent from the reference Rust CLI daemon (github.com/Cordona/claude-code-agent) — the confirmation ladder, glyph/color+ASCII-fallback convention, and dimmed-hint style were adapted from its src/domain/interactive/ module; its navigation model was NOT reusable (architecturally flat, no nested menus) and was designed fresh here

constraints: Color is decoration, never the sole signal — NO_COLOR/--no-color strips ANSI entirely
Non-TTY gates interactivity, not just styling
No visible 'Scanning...' indicator expected at this scale (~33-44 items); a 'Checking...' fallback is permitted past ~1 second, never required below it
--format=env and --format=json are both first-class in agent-facing mode
--accessible is a first-class opt-in fallback for the checklist widget
Terminal width: 80-column floor on every structural header/hint line
The no-flags wall excludes 'Non-TTY' prose callouts, which legitimately describe the non-interactive path using flag tokens
Confirmation-tier table: Selective install/Install all = Safe; Selective uninstall = Dangerous; Uninstall all = Critical (typed phrase)
The critical typed-phrase gate supplements, never replaces, the dry-run preview
Core-tier and conditional-shared-tier membership are curated, not discoverable by naming pattern alone — only the optional tier is

Every specific count/total in the document must satisfy two invariant formulas: New+Replace+Skip = discovered-optional-count (always), and (New+Replace)+conditional-shared-pulled-in+core = total-acted-on-count for install flows
'Not authenticated' renders neutral (no glyph, uncolored) everywhere except grouped inside Doctor's own Summary bullets
Every reversal/remediation line uses the mode-neutral verb 'choose', not 'select' or 'toggle'

Agent-facing mode uses a closed vocabulary: HUB_STATUS in {ok, blocked}; HUB_BLOCKED_REASON in {dependents_present, confirmation_required, dependency_unresolved, selection_required, restore_selection_required} -- the last three were added post-approval during implementation, per the specs own explicit-addition rule, never invented ad hoc: dependency_unresolved (installs dependency-resolution failure path), selection_required (a selected domain has a mandatory sub-selection and none was given), restore_selection_required (more than one CLAUDE.md backup exists and --restore-backup was not given). The spelling selection_required is normative and identical in this spec, in the domain-screens addendum and in the code; the variant subselection_required is rejected
open_questions: Exact command/binary name and install location
Exact flag spellings, including --confirm=UNINSTALL's precise form
Non-interactive default when multiple CLAUDE.md backups exist and no --restore-backup flag is given
Whether --accessible is ever auto-detected, vs. opt-in only
Visual theme specifics beyond the four semantic hues — deferred to the implementation spec
Whether 'traceability' implies a persistent multi-run history log
The exact core/conditional-shared enumerations and their sync mechanism as the framework evolves
Whether the bulk dry-run preview should eventually be grouped/columnar
